input_data.earnings_summary: Alphabet reported Q1 2024 results that exceeded analyst expectations. Total revenue reached $80.54 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Google Search & Other grew 14% to $46.16 billion. YouTube advertising revenue rose 21% to $8.09 billion. Google Cloud revenue surged 28% to $9.57 billion, reaching profitability for the first time with $900 million in operating income. Operating income grew 46% to $25.47 billion with a 31.6% operating margin. EPS came in at $1.89, beating the consensus estimate of $1.53. The board declared a $0.20 per share dividend — the first in the company's history — and authorized a $70 billion share buyback program.

key_risk_factors: Google Cloud profitability ($900M operating income) first-ever but margins still far below AWS/Azure
Search market share under threat from AI-native competitors (Perplexity, ChatGPT search)
YouTube Shorts monetization still below long-form video on a per-view basis
EU antitrust investigations into Google Search and Android advertising practices
AI integration costs (Gemini) threatening to compress advertising margins long-term
missed_signals: First-ever dividend + $70B buyback signaled management confidence in sustained cash generation
Google Cloud operating leverage inflection was more abrupt than most models predicted
